注文した (chūmon shita) means "ordered," with 注文 (chūmon) meaning "order" and した (shita) being the past tense of "to do." もの (mono) means "thing" or "item." と (to) is a particle meaning "with" or "and," used here to connect "what I ordered" with the rest of the sentence. 違います (chigaimasu) means "is different" or "is incorrect," and it is the polite form. This phrase politely indicates that the item you received is not the one you ordered.
